newsitem.title: UK: Euro-bourses hit records but dollar stalls.
newsitem.headline: Euro-bourses hit records but dollar stalls.

text.p: European stock markets followed Wall Street ever higher on Thursday, but the dollar's rise was stalled by nagging fears of central bank intervention and caution ahead of U.S. retail sales figures.

German and French shares struck yet further trading highs and London rose strongly after Wall Street leapt 1.5 percent to close overnight at a record 6,961.63 points, tantalisingly within sight of 6,700.
Foreign exchange markets were dominated in early trading by worries that the central banks of the main industrialised countries could intervene to cap the dollar's surging value.

The vice-president of the German Bundesbank, Wilhelm Gaddum, told Reuters Financial TV overnight that it was not in the bank's interest to see the dollar strengthen further, echoing a similar statement from the central bank on Wednesday.

"Generally speaking, the attitude is that on the basis of fundamentals the dollar will continue to move higher," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist for Europe at BankAmerica here. "But perhaps recent comments haven't helped the pace at which it could appreciate."
Fears of intervention have grown following the recent meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, at which the market perceived Japan to be the least pleased with the dollar's strength.
"I think if they do intervene it will certainly be on a unilateral basis," said Hawkins. "I think at the moment they are in a watch-and-wait type mode rather than wanting to intervene."
By midday the dollar was holding above 1.68 marks and 124 yen as the market also waited for the U.S. retail sales figures due at 1330 GMT.

European bond markets kicked off the day in a chirpy mood, but British government gilts retreated after stronger than expected inflation data and German bund futures also pared agins after sprinting to an all-time high.
Wall Street's massive overnight gains, propelled by the strength of the dollar and powerful inflows into U.S. mutual funds, set the tone for another bullish day in Asian and European stock markets.
In Tokyo the Nikkei rose 1.5 percent to 18,688 while European investors saw France and Germany hit fresh peaks.
Traders predicted German shares would continue their record-setting advance after the 30-shareDAX hit a record 3,232.13 points in floor trade.
"If the futures market keeps up the advance, then we could see a rally like we did on Wednesday," said one trader. German shares rose 28.56 points to 3,216.14 points in bourse trade on Wednesday.
Traders said the market found support from export sensitive shares, including carmakers such as Volkswagen AG , which was up 15.5 marks at 818 marks by midday , and BMW .
French shares were up strongly but below a fresh record of 2,631.89 at midsession ahead of the U.S. figures and after the Bank of France kept its rates unchanged.
Dealers said shares were supported by Wall Street, a strong dollar and firm bond prices.

Generale des Eaux was 4.1 percent higher on news it had been selected as industrial partner by railroad SNCF to operate its telecommunications network. This deal strengthens Generale des Eaux' Cegetel telecoms unit ahead of full competition with France Telecom in 1998.
Europe's largest stock market, London, also rose strongly in early trade but fell short of the record-breaking performance of its main rivals.

The FTSE 100 mounted an assault on the record but came to a halt at 4,329.9, just 0.1 points below its all-time high. The index turned on its heels and retreated to 4,321.1 by 1245 GMT, still 16.8 points up on the day.
Retail Price Index (RPI) data showed inflation slightly higher than expected but analysts said a near-term interest rate rise was still extremely unlikely and the FTSE ignored the news.
"We ran into resistance as we approached the record high and we just couldn't break through it," one dealer said. "Once we failed to break it we started coming off with the futures."
Annual results from Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc were well received by the market and news of a possible approach for Chubb Security Plc kept bid speculation simmering.
CURRENCIES AT 1245 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6823 marks and 124.10 yen compared with 1.6820 marks and 123.81 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1245 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 16.8 points, or 0.39 percent, at 4,321.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 22.12 points, or 0.85 percent, at 2,621.45.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 13.34 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,229.48.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $343.00 vs $337.70 previously. Silver was indicated at $5.14.
